What is the difference between contract, permanent and payroll staffing?

Permanent placement puts the worker on your payroll, and you pay the agency once. Contract staffing keeps the worker on the agency's payroll, and you pay a monthly invoice for wages, statutory dues and a service charge. Payroll outsourcing means you choose the people, and the agency only runs their salaries and compliance.

Most Tamil Nadu employers use more than one model at a time. A Sriperumbudur plant may keep its supervisors permanent and run its line helpers on contract during a model launch. A clinic in Anna Nagar may hire nurses permanently and use contract housekeeping.

When should you choose contract staffing?

Choose contract staffing when demand rises and falls, when a project has an end date, or when you want the agency to handle wages, PF, ESI and replacements. It works well for helpers, packers, housekeeping, data entry and call-centre seats where volumes change month to month.

Two rules matter. First, under the OSH Code a contractor with 50 or more contract workers needs a licence, and the principal employer has registration duties. Second, Section 57 of the OSH Code restricts contract labour in an establishment's core activities, with exceptions: work that is normally done through contractors, work that does not need full-time workers for most of the day, and sudden increases in volume that must be finished in a set time. Check how this applies to your unit with a labour-law professional.

When is permanent placement better?

Permanent placement is better for roles you will need for years and where skills build over time: supervisors, quality engineers, accountants, nurses, pharmacists, team leaders. You pay the agency once, the person joins your culture, and you avoid a monthly service charge on wages that keep running.

Ask the agency for its replacement window in writing. Market practice in India ranges from 30 to 90 days. Lifeline's terms: [replacement terms: to confirm].

What is payroll outsourcing?

Payroll outsourcing means you select the people and the agency employs them on its rolls. The agency pays salaries, deducts and deposits PF and ESI, issues payslips and files returns, and bills you monthly. It suits companies that have budget for people but no headcount approval, or a small HR team.

What about fixed-term employment?

The labour codes let you hire directly on fixed-term contracts. Fixed-term employees get the same wages and benefits as permanent staff doing the same work, and become eligible for gratuity after one year. This can replace contract staffing for some roles. It puts the worker on your payroll and your compliance.

Related questions

What is the difference between contract staffing and permanent placement?

In permanent placement the worker joins your payroll and you pay the agency a one-time fee. In contract staffing the worker stays on the agency payroll, the agency pays wages, PF and ESI, and you pay a monthly invoice. Contract suits seasonal or uncertain demand. Permanent suits long-term roles you want to own.

Does a contractor need a licence to supply contract workers in Tamil Nadu?

Under the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, in force since 21 November 2025, a contractor engaging 50 or more contract workers needs a licence. The old law set the threshold at 20. State rules decide the procedure, so ask any agency for its licence and check the current Tamil Nadu rules with your labour-law adviser.

Is payroll outsourcing the same as contract staffing?

Not quite. In payroll outsourcing you find and select the people yourself, and the agency only holds them on its payroll and handles salary, PF, ESI and statutory filings. In contract staffing the agency also sources, screens and replaces the workers. Payroll outsourcing usually costs less because there is no recruiting work.
